skill.name: Writing Hookify Rules
skill.description: Guides users in creating Hookify rules that watch Claude Code events and show warnings or block unsafe actions.
skill.summary: Create focused Hookify rules for Claude Code events and workflow checks.
skill.author: CaptainCrouton89

security_audit.summary: Static detections are false positives from Markdown examples and protective rule patterns; the skill does not itself execute destructive commands or access secrets. However, its documented dynamic interpolation feature can execute arbitrary local commands from rule messages. Publish only with clear safeguards for command interpolation.

remediation.issue: Dynamic message interpolation can run arbitrary shell commands.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit confirmation before executing interpolated commands and restrict them to an allowlist.

remediation.issue: Command output can expose data to the model context.
remediation.suggestion: Redact secrets, limit output size, and warn users not to interpolate credential-bearing commands.
Recommend project-local rules by default and explain the broader effect of global rules.

static_findings.snippet: Hookify rules are markdown files with YAML frontmatter that define patterns to watch for and message
- `teammate_idle`: When a teammate is about to go idle
- `task_completed`: When a task is marked complete
- `block`: Prevent operation (PreToolUse), stop session (Stop), force continuation (TeammateIdle), o
- YAML quoted strings: `"pattern"` requires double backslashes `\\s`

semantic_findings.title: Unrestricted Dynamic Command Interpolation
semantic_findings.description: The skill documents message syntax that executes shell commands and inserts their output. A user-created rule can therefore run arbitrary local commands when its event triggers.

content.value_statement: Hookify rules can enforce repeatable checks during Claude Code work. This skill explains rule structure, event matching, and useful warning patterns.
actual_capabilities: Explains the Markdown and YAML structure of a Hookify rule.
Describes Bash, file, stop, prompt, teammate, and task events.
Shows single-pattern and multi-condition matching examples.
Explains Python-style regular expressions and YAML escaping.
Suggests rules for dangerous commands, sensitive files, and completion checks.
Documents project-local and global rule file locations.
limitations: It provides guidance only and does not install or validate rules.
Regex examples may require adjustment for a specific project.
Dynamic command interpolation can execute local commands and needs separate safeguards.
Hookify behavior depends on the installed Hookify implementation.

use_cases.title: Protect risky shell actions
use_cases.description: Create a Bash event rule that warns before destructive or privileged commands run.

use_cases.title: Check sensitive file edits
use_cases.description: Create a file event rule that highlights edits to environment or credential files.

use_cases.title: Enforce completion checks
use_cases.description: Create a stop event rule that reminds an agent to run tests and update documentation.

prompt_templates.title: Create a basic warning
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Hookify Bash rule that warns when a command contains rm -rf. Use a descriptive name and explain each field.

prompt_templates.title: Guard environment edits
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Hookify file rule that warns when API_KEY is added to a .env file. Use multiple conditions.

prompt_templates.title: Add a release checklist
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a stop event rule that blocks completion until tests, build status, and documentation are checked.

prompt_templates.title: Design scoped safeguards
prompt_templates.prompt: Design three project-local Hookify rules for shell safety, sensitive files, and production deployment prompts. Explain the regex choices.

output_examples.input: Create a rule that warns before sudo commands.
output: Message: Explain that elevated permissions require review.

output_examples.input: Create a completion rule for documentation.
output: Message: Ask whether documentation was updated.

best_practices: Use narrow patterns that match the intended command or file change.
Store project-specific rules in the project-local Hookify directory.
Use warnings first, then use blocking rules only for well-tested cases.
anti_patterns: Do not use broad patterns that match unrelated text.
Do not place secrets or credentials in rule messages.
Do not use dynamic command interpolation without confirmation and output controls.

faq.question: What is a Hookify rule?
faq.answer: It is a Markdown file with YAML frontmatter that reacts to selected agent events.

faq.question: Which events can a rule watch?
faq.answer: The skill documents Bash, file, stop, prompt, teammate idle, task completed, and all events.

faq.question: Can a rule block an action?
faq.answer: Yes. A rule can use the block action when the Hookify event supports blocking.

faq.question: Where should I store a project rule?
faq.answer: Store it under the project .claude directory using the documented Hookify local filename pattern.

faq.question: How do I test a regex?
faq.answer: Test it with representative text before relying on it in a rule.

faq.question: Are dynamic commands safe?
faq.answer: Treat them carefully. They can execute local commands and may expose command output to the model context.
